summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, prior CABG, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and a previous stroke was admitted for evaluation of substernal chest pain radiating to the left shoulder, occurring during physical activity and emotional stress. Initial concerns for acute coronary syndrome were ruled out by normal cardiac enzymes, unchanged EKG, and no acute findings on chest X-ray. The pain was reproducible on chest wall palpation, leading to a diagnosis of costochondritis. Her blood pressure was elevated on admission, likely due to medication noncompliance, and improved with reinitiation of home antihypertensives. She remained on her baseline medications for diabetes, hyperlipidemia, asthma, and depression. She was discharged home with instructions to use acetaminophen for pain, continue all chronic medications, and follow up with her primary care provider and cardiologist.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
